newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Matutes rejects boycott of French goods.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Matutes rejects boycott of French goods.

text.p: Spanish Foreign Minister Abel Matutes rejected on Wednesday demands from angry farmers for a boycott of French products in reprisal for attacks on Spanish truckers importing vegetables and fruits to France.

The boycott call came after a week in which French farmers repeatedly dumped and destroyed Spanish produce coming in by truck or already stored in warehouses. The French farmers want tighter controls on cheaper imported vegetables and fruits.
"There is no reason why all French people, the French nation, should have to pay for the violent abuses of a few fanatics against whom we demand the full weight of the law," Matutes told reporters.
"It would be unfair and...it would be counterproductive. Let us not forget that Spain has its best customers in France," he added.

Matutes said at the weekend that he had demanded "severe sanctions" by the European Union to punish France for Spanish farmers' losses, estimated at tens of billions of pesetas. Spanish officials say the attacks jeapordise a single European market.
Spain has accused French police of standing by passively while the attacks went on. France apologised to Spain last week and promised to take action to prevent further aggression.
